items.definition: Used to say what is really true, often when it is different from what someone expects or thinks.
examples: I thought the film would be boring, but it was actually quite funny.
Actually, I'd rather not go out tonight.

trap.en: Actually does not mean 'at the present time'. For that, use currently, at the moment or nowadays: I'm currently living in Leeds.
trap.es: Actually no es «actualmente». Significa «en realidad» o «de hecho». Para «actualmente» di currently, at the moment o nowadays.

items.definition: After a long time, or after a lot of delay or effort; in the end.
examples: After three hours on the motorway, we eventually reached the coast.
She eventually found a flat she could afford.

trap.en: Eventually is not 'possibly' or 'occasionally'. It means that something happens at last, after a delay. For 'possibly', use possibly or perhaps; for 'occasionally', use from time to time.
trap.es: Eventually no es «eventualmente» (posiblemente, de forma ocasional). Es «al final» o «con el tiempo»: algo ocurre por fin, tras una espera.

items.definition: Showing good judgement and likely to make practical, reasonable choices.
examples: It would be sensible to book the train tickets early.
He's a very sensible driver and never takes risks.

trap.en: Sensible does not mean easily hurt or emotional. That is sensitive: She is very sensitive to criticism.
trap.es: Sensible en inglés es «sensato», no «sensible». Para «sensible» (que se ofende o siente mucho) usa sensitive.

items.definition: Feeling uncomfortable or ashamed because of something that has happened in front of other people.
examples: I was so embarrassed when I forgot my manager's name.
He felt embarrassed about his poor English.

trap.en: Embarrassed has nothing to do with pregnancy. A pregnant woman is pregnant or expecting a baby.
trap.es: I'm embarrassed es «me da vergüenza», no «estoy embarazada». Embarazada se dice pregnant.

items.definition: To help someone do something, especially in a formal or professional way.
examples: A volunteer will assist you with your registration.
Please contact reception if we can assist you in any way.

trap.en: Assist means help. To be present at a meeting, class or event, use attend: I attended the conference, not I assisted the conference.
trap.es: «Asistir a una reunión» es attend. Assist significa «ayudar», y es más formal que help.

items.definition: To be present at an event, meeting, class or place where something takes place.
examples: Over two hundred people attended the opening ceremony.
She attends evening classes twice a week.

trap.en: Attend is not 'to serve or look after someone'. For a customer, say serve or deal with: The shop assistant served me quickly. Attend a meeting means to go to it.
trap.es: Attend es «asistir a», no «atender». «Atender a un cliente» es serve o deal with a customer.

items.definition: A building or room where books and other materials are kept for people to read or borrow.
examples: I borrowed three novels from the local library.
The university library is open until midnight during exams.
collocations: borrow a book from the library

trap.en: A library lends books; a shop that sells them is a bookshop (in the US, a bookstore).
trap.es: Library es «biblioteca», no «librería». Una librería, donde se compran libros, es a bookshop.

items.definition: To understand or notice something suddenly, often something you had not seen before.
examples: I realised halfway to work that I had left my phone at home.
He didn't realise how late it was.

trap.en: Realise means to become aware of something. To carry out a task or a plan, use do, carry out or complete: We carried out a survey.
trap.es: Realise es «darse cuenta», no «realizar». «Realizar un estudio» es carry out a study o do a study.

items.definition: A thick covering for a whole floor, usually fixed in place and made of wool or a similar material.
examples: We're going to replace the carpet in the living room.
Red wine spilt on a pale carpet is almost impossible to remove.

trap.en: A carpet is on the floor. The thing you keep papers in is a folder (or a file).
trap.es: Carpet es «moqueta» o «alfombra», no «carpeta». Una carpeta de papeles es a folder.

items.definition: A way out of a building, room or motorway; also the act of leaving a place.
examples: The nearest exit is at the end of the corridor.
Take the next exit for the airport.

trap.en: Exit means the way out. Do not use it for achievement: the word you want is success.

items.definition: An agreement in which each side gives up something it wanted so that both can accept the result.
examples: After a long discussion, we reached a compromise on the budget.
Neither side was willing to compromise.

trap.en: Compromise is not a commitment or an obligation. For a duty or promise use commitment; for an arranged meeting use appointment. A compromise means both sides give way a little.
trap.es: Compromise es «llegar a un acuerdo cediendo cada parte», no «compromiso» como obligación (commitment) ni cita (appointment).

items.definition: To help someone by giving encouragement, money or practical help, or to agree with an idea or a cause.
examples: My parents supported me throughout my studies.
Most residents support the plan for a new cycle lane.

trap.en: Support does not mean to put up with something unpleasant. For that, use stand or put up with: I can't stand the noise.
trap.es: Support es «apoyar» o «mantener», no «soportar» (aguantar). «No soporto el ruido» es I can't stand the noise.

items.definition: The achievement of what you wanted to do; something that turns out well.
examples: The festival was a huge success this year.
Hard work is the key to success.

trap.en: Success is not an event or incident. For something that happened, say event, incident or occurrence.
trap.es: Success es «éxito», no «suceso». Un suceso (algo que ocurre) es an event o an incident.

items.definition: To talk about a subject with someone in order to share ideas or reach a decision.
examples: We need to discuss the schedule before the meeting.
The committee will discuss the proposal next week.

trap.en: Discuss is a calm exchange of ideas. A heated quarrel is to argue or to have an argument. Also, discuss takes a direct object: discuss the plan, not discuss about the plan.
trap.es: Discuss es «hablar de algo», no «discutir» (pelearse), que se dice argue. Además, no lleva about: discuss the plan.

items.definition: An angry disagreement between people; also a set of reasons given to support an opinion.
examples: My brother and I had an argument about whose turn it was to cook.
There is a strong argument for working from home two days a week.

trap.en: In everyday English an argument is usually a quarrel. The story of a film or book is the plot.
trap.es: Argument suele ser «discusión» o «riña». El argumento de una película o novela es the plot.
